plants.name: Asplenium nidus 'Crispy Wave'
plants.tip: Water the compost, never the central cup. Water left standing in the crown rots it.
plants.colour: Mid-green, deeply rippled fronds held upright

plants.name: Asplenium nidus 'Crissie'
plants.tip: Keep the rosette out of draughts. Cold moving air scorches new fronds brown at the tip.
plants.colour: Light green with forked, crested frond tips

plants.name: Asplenium nidus 'Fimbriatum'
plants.tip: Old fronds brown from the tip inwards. Cut them off at the base rather than trimming edges.
plants.colour: Mid-green with finely fringed, lacerated margins

plants.name: Asplenium nidus 'Plicatum'
plants.tip: Dust settles in the pleats and blocks light. Wipe the fronds with a damp cloth monthly.
plants.colour: Deep green, heavily pleated along the length

plants.name: Asplenium nidus 'Leslie'
plants.tip: The crested tips only form properly in humid air. In a dry room the fronds come plain.
plants.colour: Glossy green with branched, curled frond tips

plants.name: Asplenium nidus 'Cobra'
plants.tip: Pour at the pot edge and let the top centimetre dry before watering again.
plants.colour: Dark green, narrow and twisted with wavy edges

plants.name: Asplenium nidus 'Campio'
plants.tip: The compact rosette traps water easily. Water at the rim and empty the saucer afterwards.
plants.colour: Bright green, broad and wavy in a tight rosette

plants.name: Asplenium nidus 'Avis'
plants.tip: Direct sun bleaches the fronds pale yellow, and that damage never grows out of a frond.
plants.colour: Mid-green strap fronds with strongly waved edges

plants.name: Asplenium antiquum
plants.tip: Takes cooler rooms than most bird's nest ferns, but still will not tolerate a wet crown.
plants.colour: Glossy mid-green, upright and slightly rippled

plants.name: Asplenium antiquum 'Osaka'
plants.tip: Feed at half strength. Ferns scorch at the frond edges on full-rate fertiliser.
plants.colour: Deep green, narrow with tightly waved margins

plants.name: Asplenium antiquum 'Victoria'
plants.tip: New fronds unfurl from the centre. Never pull at them, as they snap and do not regrow.
plants.colour: Mid-green, long and tapering with wavy edges

plants.name: Asplenium antiquum 'Hurricane'
plants.tip: The twist in the frond tightens in good light and slackens off in a dim corner.
plants.colour: Bright green fronds twisted along their length

plants.name: Asplenium australasicum (crow's nest fern)
plants.tip: It gets large. Give it a wide, shallow pot and a metre of clear space around it.
plants.colour: Mid-green, broad, with a dark keel underneath

plants.name: Asplenium serratum
plants.tip: Wants steady warmth above 15°C. Cold wet compost in winter is what usually kills it.
plants.colour: Apple green with a sawtoothed frond margin

plants.name: Asplenium musifolium
plants.tip: It grows on trees in the wild, so use an open bark-based mix rather than dense compost.
plants.colour: Broad pale-green fronds with a black midrib

plants.name: Asplenium bulbiferum (mother spleenwort)
plants.tip: The bulbils on the fronds root themselves if pressed onto damp compost while still attached.
plants.colour: Finely divided, soft mid-green lace

plants.name: Asplenium x lucrosum
plants.tip: Sterile, so it spreads by plantlets rather than spores. Keep it evenly moist all year.
plants.colour: Fine, feathery mid-green with narrow segments

plants.name: Asplenium 'Austral Gem'
plants.tip: The one Asplenium that copes with ordinary room humidity, though not with dry roots.
plants.colour: Glossy dark green, leathery and finely cut

plants.name: Asplenium 'Parvati'
plants.tip: Slow to establish. Leave it in the same pot for two years before moving it on.
plants.colour: Dark glossy green, more finely divided than Austral Gem

plants.name: Asplenium daucifolium (Mauritius mother fern)
plants.tip: Plantlets form along the fronds. Peg one into compost and cut it free once it has rooted.
plants.colour: Very finely divided mid-green, almost carrot-like

plants.name: Asplenium dimorphum
plants.tip: Needs warmth and shade. The fronds crisp within days of direct afternoon sun.
plants.colour: Two frond types: broad sterile, thread-like fertile

plants.name: Asplenium oblongifolium (shining spleenwort)
plants.tip: Tolerates a cool room down to about 5°C, but wants shade and compost that never dries.
plants.colour: Glossy dark green with long, pointed pinnae

plants.name: Asplenium scolopendrium (hart's tongue fern)
plants.tip: A shade plant. Full sun turns the glossy straps yellow and papery within one season.
plants.colour: Glossy strap-shaped fronds, bright green

plants.name: Asplenium scolopendrium 'Angustatum'
plants.tip: Cut last year's fronds back in early spring so the new croziers come up unshaded.
plants.colour: Narrow, strap-like glossy green fronds

plants.name: Asplenium scolopendrium 'Crispum'
plants.tip: Sterile, so it never self-sows. Divide the crown in spring if you want more of it.
plants.colour: Bright green with tightly frilled, wavy margins

plants.name: Asplenium scolopendrium 'Undulatum'
plants.tip: Prefers alkaline soil. A little lime or grit suits it far better than an ericaceous mix.
plants.colour: Glossy green with a strongly waved edge

plants.name: Asplenium scolopendrium 'Cristatum'
plants.tip: The crested tips fade out on a hungry plant. Keep it fed and the branching holds.
plants.colour: Glossy green with a forked, crested tip

plants.name: Asplenium scolopendrium 'Kaye's Lacerated'
plants.tip: Slow growing, so do not overpot it. A snug pot and steady moisture suit it best.
plants.colour: Broad green fronds with torn, jagged edges

plants.name: Asplenium scolopendrium 'Marginatum'
plants.tip: Take browned fronds off at the base in spring. Once marked, a frond will not recover.
plants.colour: Green fronds with a narrow lobed frill at the margin

plants.name: Asplenium scolopendrium 'Muricatum'
plants.tip: The rough surface traps dust and grit. Rinse the fronds under a cool tap now and then.
plants.colour: Rough-textured green with a puckered surface

plants.name: Asplenium scolopendrium 'Ramocristatum'
plants.tip: Give it room. The branched tips tangle and rot where the crown is crowded and damp.
plants.colour: Green fronds branching into many crested tips

plants.name: Asplenium scolopendrium 'Peraferens'
plants.tip: Buds along the frond root readily. Lay a frond on damp compost and weight it down.
plants.colour: Narrow green fronds carrying small proliferous buds

plants.name: Asplenium scolopendrium 'Crispum Bolton's Nobile'
plants.tip: One of the slowest hart's tongues. Feed lightly and never let the roots dry out.
plants.colour: Deep green with broad, evenly frilled margins

plants.name: Asplenium trichomanes (maidenhair spleenwort)
plants.tip: A crevice fern. Grow it in gritty, limy compost and water it from below.
plants.colour: Black wiry stems with small, round green pinnae

plants.name: Asplenium trichomanes 'Incisum'
plants.tip: Small and slow. A shallow pan of gritty compost suits it better than a deep pot.
plants.colour: Black stems with deeply cut, toothed pinnae

plants.name: Asplenium ceterach (rustyback fern)
plants.tip: Drought adapted. It curls up shut when dry and reopens when watered, so never keep it soggy.
plants.colour: Green above, dense rust-brown scales beneath

plants.name: Asplenium platyneuron (ebony spleenwort)
plants.tip: Wants drier shade than most ferns. Let the top of the compost dry between waterings.
plants.colour: Dark glossy stems with narrow green pinnae

plants.name: Asplenium x ebenoides (Scott's spleenwort)
plants.tip: A limestone hybrid. Add grit and a little lime, and keep the crown clear of standing wet.
plants.colour: Irregular green blades on a dark, shining stem

plants.name: Asplenium x ebenoides 'Dragontail'
plants.tip: It resents division. Increase it from spores or buy another rather than splitting the crown.
plants.colour: Long tapering green blades with lobed edges

plants.name: Asplenium flabellifolium (necklace fern)
plants.tip: The trailing tips root where they touch compost. Pin one down to start a new plant.
plants.colour: Trailing fronds of small fan-shaped green segments
